30jNsCVLpAE.summary: Bryan Cantrill's GOTO Chicago 2017 talk on debugging production systems under pressure, centered on the incident where an operator's mistyped command rebooted an entire Joyent datacenter. It covers human factors, automation and architecture.
30jNsCVLpAE.why: A perennial HN recommendation for outage and postmortem threads, praised as funny, educational and one of the best postmortems anyone has seen.

36myc8wQhLo.summary: Timothy Roscoe of ETH Zurich delivers the joint USENIX ATC/OSDI 2021 keynote arguing that operating systems must reckon with modern hardware, which is a heterogeneous collection of processors, firmware and coprocessors rather than a simple machine. It shows how much runs below and beside Linux.
36myc8wQhLo.why: Repeatedly recommended as a revelatory talk on how little control the main OS has over modern SoCs and PCs.

3LopI4YeC4I.summary: Veritasium examines the role of luck in success, with simulations and examples showing how small advantages and chance can compound. It argues that top outcomes are disproportionately luck-driven while still crediting effort.
3LopI4YeC4I.why: Linked in threads about meritocracy, careers and startups as a reminder that luck shapes who ends up on top.

3kEfedtQVOY.summary: Meredith Patterson and Sergey Bratus argue that networked software stays insecure because protocols and inputs are too complex to recognize safely. They propose using formal language theory and grammars to build secure, verifiable input handling.
3kEfedtQVOY.why: HN commenters call it one of the best security talks and the standard introduction to LANGSEC, which they use to argue for simpler, well-specified input formats.

3nwwKbM_vJc.summary: Jon Kabat-Zinn leads an hour-long Google tech talk on mindfulness, introducing the basic ideas and including a guided meditation. It is aimed at newcomers.
3nwwKbM_vJc.why: For over a decade HN has pointed people asking about stress, focus or meditation to this as a restful and approachable introduction to mindfulness.

3Y3jE3B8HsE.summary: A short CGP Grey explainer on the alternative vote (instant runoff voting) versus first past the post, made around the 2011 UK referendum. It shows how ranked ballots are tallied and why they avoid spoiler effects.
3Y3jE3B8HsE.why: HN's go-to link whenever ranked-choice voting or voting reform comes up, because it explains the mechanics quickly and entertainingly.

3Ea3pkTCYx4.summary: A short animated simulation comparing how Multics and Unix were developed, showing why Unix's small composable programs and pipes gave it a efficiency advantage. It frames Unix as a moonshot achievable by a small team.
3Ea3pkTCYx4.why: Cited constantly in threads on microservices, composability and the Unix philosophy as a compact explanation of why small interoperable pieces win.

3kEpZWGgJks.summary: John Oliver's Last Week Tonight segment on civil asset forfeiture, the process by which police can seize property they suspect is tied to crime. It explains how the property itself is put on trial and how departments profit.
3kEpZWGgJks.why: HN treats it as the standard accessible explainer on civil forfeiture, linked in nearly every thread about police seizures.

3wfNl2L0Gf8.summary: The full 1971 Dutch television debate between Noam Chomsky and Michel Foucault on human nature, with subtitles. They discuss creativity, knowledge, power and politics.
3wfNl2L0Gf8.why: HN recommends it as a famous, revealing clash between two thinkers, though some note they largely talk past each other.

3Fx5Q8xGU8k.summary: Peter Thiel's lecture from the How to Start a Startup course on business strategy and monopoly theory, arguing that competition destroys profits and that startups should aim to build monopolies. It covers the ideas of Zero to One.
3Fx5Q8xGU8k.why: HN recommends it as a serious, influential talk on market size and monopoly, though some commenters criticize its philosophy as endorsing anti-competitive goals.

3VQ382QG-y4.summary: Gabriel Lebec's Fullstack Academy talk introduces lambda calculus syntax, the history of mathematical logic, and the essence of functional programming using JavaScript. It also covers combinators, currying and Church encodings.
3VQ382QG-y4.why: Repeatedly recommended as one of the most approachable introductions to lambda calculus and combinators.

3ZTGwcHQfLY.summary: Destin Sandlin of Smarter Every Day tries to manufacture a grill scrubber entirely in the United States. Along the way he runs into missing supply chains, tooling and institutional manufacturing knowledge.
3ZTGwcHQfLY.why: HN cites it constantly in US manufacturing debates as a vivid demonstration of how much domestic industrial capability has been lost.

36GT2zI8lVA.summary: A short clip of Richard Feynman answering an interviewer's question about why magnets repel, explaining that a 'why' question depends on a shared framework of understanding. It illustrates how hard it is to explain fundamentals to a layperson.
36GT2zI8lVA.why: Cited constantly as the classic answer to 'why' questions, on explanation, frames of reference and the limits of physics.

3VZSJKbzyMc.summary: Fools & Dreamers is a 30-minute documentary about Hinewai Nature Reserve in New Zealand, where botanist Hugh Wilson let gorse grow as a nurse canopy to regenerate native forest. It shows the results after 30 years and the local skepticism he faced.
3VZSJKbzyMc.why: Shared in climate and land-use threads as a vivid example of how letting land regrow can restore forest.

3-son3EJTrU.summary: An RSA Animate in which Steven Pinker explains how the mind builds infinite meanings from finite language, and why people often speak indirectly. It covers ambiguity, politeness and mutual knowledge, including the emperor's new clothes example.
3-son3EJTrU.why: HN recommends it as a short, clear explanation of why people avoid saying things explicitly and how common knowledge works socially and politically.

34LGPIXvU5M.summary: A short Al Jazeera animation narrated by Amy Goodman presenting Noam Chomsky's five filters of the mass media: ownership, advertising, media elite sourcing, flak and a common enemy. It is part of the MediaTheorised series.
34LGPIXvU5M.why: HN recommends it as a quick, accessible introduction to the propaganda model from Manufacturing Consent.

3GJUM6pCpew.summary: Matt Parker explains the history behind NTSC television running at 29.97 frames per second rather than 30, tracing it to the backward-compatible addition of color. He walks through the arithmetic behind the odd ratio.
3GJUM6pCpew.why: Go-to explanation whenever the strange 29.97 frame rate comes up, praised for its clarity and presenter.

3GVO-MfIl1Q.summary: Skateboarding pioneer Rodney Mullen talks about how the open skate community and its environments drive the invention of new tricks out of pure passion. He draws parallels to collaboration and open source.
3GVO-MfIl1Q.why: HN people share it as an inspiring talk linking skateboarding creativity to hacking and open-source knowledge sharing.

3dl9Ovwmnxw.summary: A short video on the US Sprint anti-ballistic missile, which accelerated to around Mach 10 in seconds under extreme g-forces and heat. It includes striking launch footage and a brief development history.
3dl9Ovwmnxw.why: Shared in hypersonic and missile threads as a compact, impressive overview of what Sprint achieved in the 1960s.

3s7h2MHQtxc.summary: 3Blue1Brown explains space-filling curves and the Hilbert curve, and how infinite mathematical constructions connect to finite, practical approximations. It touches on mapping between dimensions and sensory ideas.
3s7h2MHQtxc.why: Recommended as the best visual introduction to Hilbert curves, which come up in indexing, image layout and dimensionality mapping.

39iKLwlUqBo.summary: A short clip of Steve Jobs at the 2010 D8 conference, interviewed by Walt Mossberg, defining privacy as people knowing what they are signing up for, in plain English and repeatedly. The discussion centered on location data.
39iKLwlUqBo.why: HN reaches for it constantly as evidence of Apple's long-standing privacy stance and as a yardstick for judging Apple, Facebook and others.

3BR8tK-LuB0.summary: Numberphile's James Grime introduces quaternions, a type of number beyond the complex numbers, building up from real and complex numbers and explaining why they are useful.
3BR8tK-LuB0.why: HN recommends it as the simplest, most approachable introduction to quaternions, useful for people working in games and robotics.

3GObi93tjZI.summary: David Guillot describes how his team replaced a two-year-old React UI of their SaaS product with Django templates and htmx in a couple of months. The talk gives concrete indicators on code size, performance and team impact.
3GObi93tjZI.why: HN commenters point to it as a real-world case study of moving from React to htmx, especially in threads on boring web development and HTML over the wire.

3ka4KY7TMTU.summary: David Ungar of IBM Research reflects at Stanford on the Self language project and argues the real legacy of ideas is the people. He covers its history, philosophy, successes and failures.
3ka4KY7TMTU.why: HN points to it as the best account of what Self made possible and what its team went on to do.

3lXv3Tt4x20.summary: Linguist Simon Roper reconstructs how a London accent would have sounded from the 14th to the 21st centuries, reading passages in period pronunciation. It draws on the Cambridge History of the English Language.
3lXv3Tt4x20.why: HN recommends it as a captivating, accessible tour of how English pronunciation changed, including the rise and fall of the rhotic r.

3uiEyEKji0M.summary: Andrew Adams, a Halide developer, presents the Halide language for image processing and tensor computation. The talk explains the separation of algorithm from schedule with illustrated examples of parallelism, locality and redundancy tradeoffs.
3uiEyEKji0M.why: Recommended as the clearest explanation of Halide's ideas and of scheduling for performance.

35Idb_lCU4o.summary: A Ninja Nerd whiteboard lecture on the Moderna, Pfizer/BioNTech and AstraZeneca COVID-19 vaccines. It covers how each works, the preclinical and phase I-III trial process, and Operation Warp Speed.
35Idb_lCU4o.why: HN recommended it in late 2020 as a detailed, science-based explanation of how the different vaccines work and how they were tested.

37wFVVVZlVU.summary: A panel with Tony Hoare, Joe Armstrong and Carl Hewitt, hosted by Francesco Cesarini, on the history and future of concurrency. The three creators of CSP, Erlang and the actor model discuss their differing approaches.
37wFVVVZlVU.why: HN recommends it for getting the inventors of major concurrency models together, disagreements included.

3EPTfOTC4Jw.summary: NCommander investigates why Space Cadet Pinball disappeared from Windows Vista, building on Raymond Chen's explanation about 64-bit incompatibility. He tests it on 64-bit Windows including Itanium and walks through the debugging.
3EPTfOTC4Jw.why: Recommended as the detailed, entertaining history of why 3D Pinball vanished from Windows.

3FOzD4Sfgag.summary: An Every Frame a Painting video essay analysing how Edgar Wright creates visual comedy through framing, camera movement, editing, sound effects and music.
3FOzD4Sfgag.why: Recommended as a short, eye-opening piece of film analysis whenever physical or visual comedy is discussed.

3LVeEjsn8Ts.summary: Hennessy and Patterson's 2018 Turing Award lecture at ISCA, A New Golden Age for Computer Architecture. It covers domain-specific hardware, security, open instruction sets and agile chip development.
3LVeEjsn8Ts.why: HN repeatedly recommends it as the best overview of the past, present and future of chip performance after Moore's law.

3TFz1xqp3us.summary: A first-day ride-along with an Amazon delivery driver using the Rivian electric delivery van. She covers the van's new technology, how it compares to the standard Ford Transit delivery vehicles, and quirks and issues she noticed on the job.
3TFz1xqp3us.why: HN points to it as a rare review from an actual delivery driver rather than a car reviewer, showing how the van's design suits the job.

3TX3kV3TICU.summary: George Brocklehurst of thoughtbot demonstrates Vim's built-in completion mechanisms, from word, line and block completion to ctags. The aim is to type less and make fewer typos.
3TX3kV3TICU.why: HN users say it made Vim's completion system click for them.

3WMuzhQXJoY.summary: Documentary filmmaker Cassie Jaye explains how making The Red Pill led her, a feminist, to reevaluate her assumptions about the Men's Rights movement. She argues for listening to people you think of as the enemy.
3WMuzhQXJoY.why: HN recommends it as a thoughtful account from a feminist on men's issues and the cost of saying unpopular things.

3qln2u1Vr2E.summary: Eric Brandwine's AWS re:Invent 2015 session on how Amazon VPC networking works. It covers the problems the design solved, why traditional approaches do not scale, and the mechanisms used for customer isolation and VPC endpoints.
3qln2u1Vr2E.why: Considered a favorite deep dive into how AWS does virtual networking at L3 and why VPC hosts cannot snoop each other.

3x1b_S6Qp2Q.summary: Lex Fridman interviews Ethereum co-creator Vitalik Buterin about Ethereum, cryptocurrency and the future of money. The conversation also touches on technical topics such as quantum computing and mining.
3x1b_S6Qp2Q.why: HN recommends it as a fascinating conversation showing how the Ethereum founder thinks.

31D94QOo2gY.summary: A DEF CON 21 talk by Karl Koscher and Eric Butler on how SIM cards work, including Java Card applets, the SIM toolkit and the OS running on the card. It shows how much control the network and the card have independent of the phone.
31D94QOo2gY.why: HN cites it as the go-to overview of what SIM cards can run and do, usually in threads about Java Card, SIM attacks or phone security.

3DtUzH3zoFo.summary: Rob Pike's 2010 talk at OSCON's Emerging Languages Camp on where Go's concurrency style comes from. It traces the idea from Hoare's CSP through Squeak, Newsqueak and Limbo to Go.
3DtUzH3zoFo.why: HN recommends it as the clearest account of the CSP lineage behind Go's goroutines and channels.

3Gmex_4hreQ.summary: A two-minute demonstration of the loudness war, showing how heavy dynamic range compression in CD mastering makes music louder while degrading sound quality. It uses audio examples so you can hear the distortion.
3Gmex_4hreQ.why: HN keeps linking it as the shortest clear explanation of over-compression and brickwalled mastering.

3HxVMGaiZbc.summary: David Nolen explains how ClojureScript is used at Vouch.io to build mobile and web software with a single language and REPL-driven workflow. The talk includes a live coding demo of React Native development.
3HxVMGaiZbc.why: Pointed to as a concrete demonstration of REPL-driven development and ClojureScript with React Native.

3Y2weLDiUWw.summary: Erik Demaine's MIT 6.851 Advanced Data Structures lecture introducing succinct data structures, covering rank, select and tries. It is part of the Spring 2012 course.
3Y2weLDiUWw.why: HN recommends it as a clear, high-quality introduction to succinct data structures from a leading authority.

31CcclqEiZw.summary: An Intelligence Squared debate in which Will Self argues for Brave New World and Adam Gopnik for Nineteen Eighty-Four as the better dystopian warning. It includes acted excerpts and is chaired by Jonathan Freedland.
31CcclqEiZw.why: HN recommends it as a good long debate for the recurring question of whether Orwell or Huxley was right.

37iHSwA1SwE.summary: A short Yes Minister clip in which the civil servant explains why Britain joined the European Union, delivered as satire of British foreign policy.
37iHSwA1SwE.why: HN posts it, often jokingly, as a prescient and witty explanation of Britain's ambivalent stance toward Europe, especially around Brexit.

3CWCqJl0BEs.summary: Doug DeMuro reviews the Rivian electric delivery van built for Amazon, walking through its quirks, features and design innovations. It is a long, detailed tour of the vehicle inside and out.
3CWCqJl0BEs.why: HN points to it as the most thorough walkthrough of the Amazon Rivian van, useful for seeing its real size and delivery-specific design.

3Hdn0MuCK_0.summary: Electronics hobbyist bigclivedotcom tears down a cheap USB power supply with a manufacturing fault that carries full mains voltage to the USB ports, showing the risk of electric shock.
3Hdn0MuCK_0.why: Cited in threads about cheap chargers as proof of why proper certified and isolated power supplies are worth paying for.

3MghYhf-GhU.summary: A Computer History Museum oral history panel with four 3dfx founders on the company's rise with Voodoo Graphics and Glide, and its fall into bankruptcy. It runs about two and a half hours.
3MghYhf-GhU.why: Recommended as the definitive retrospective on 3dfx, with first-hand stories about engineering hacks and design philosophy.

34rdxDgpaaA.summary: An episode of the Well There's Your Problem podcast on the 1987 Goiania radiological accident in Brazil, based largely on the IAEA report. It goes through the event day by day.
34rdxDgpaaA.why: HN points to it as a good, detailed podcast account whenever the Goiania incident or lost radioactive sources come up.

36qZYL5RlgY.summary: Netflix engineer Drew Gallatin's EuroBSDcon 2022 talk quantifies the older FreeBSD optimizations that let Netflix serve web traffic at 800Gb/s, including TSO, LRO, VM page cache zones, asynchronous sendfile and unmapped mbufs.
36qZYL5RlgY.why: HN points to it as the recorded talk behind the Netflix 800Gb/s slides and as a deep look at kernel-level optimizations for high throughput.

37NaHRE0Sqw.summary: A Google Tech Talk by the author of Kilim, a Java library for lightweight actor-style message passing. It argues that message passing can replace shared-memory concurrency and claims performance competitive with or better than Erlang for huge numbers of actors.
37NaHRE0Sqw.why: Pointed to as evidence that Java can do fast, cheap message-passing concurrency, as an alternative to Erlang or Scala actors.

3BJU2drrtCM.summary: The Slow Mo Guys film a TV and screens with a high-speed camera to show how displays build an image. The footage includes CRT-style scanning and how pixels light up over time.
3BJU2drrtCM.why: Frequently linked as visual proof of how a CRT's raster scan and phosphor decay work.

3HROqnw-nf4.summary: A CppCon 2014 talk from Microsoft engineers on using portable single-source C++ to deliver Office across iOS, Android, Windows and Mac. It covers architectures, techniques and lessons from real cross-platform projects.
3HROqnw-nf4.why: Cited as evidence that large production apps share a C++ core with native UI, in cross-platform and React Native or Flutter debates.

3IryIOyPfTE.summary: A short documentary about Eric Maundu's Arduino-controlled aquaponics setup in West Oakland, where contaminated soil rules out ordinary farming. Fish and circulating water grow plants without soil.
3IryIOyPfTE.why: HN cites it as a neat example of urban aquaponics and as a plausible alternative path for people leaving programming.

3QnD2c4Xovk.summary: A short Art of the Problem clip explaining Diffie-Hellman key exchange, using a paint mixing analogy for one-way functions and touching on modular arithmetic and discrete logarithms.
3QnD2c4Xovk.why: Recommended as a simple, non-mathematical way to understand key exchange.

3R3-YwDZrzg.summary: Footage of British steeplejack Fred Dibnah climbing a chimney overhang at over fifty years old, without a harness. It is a short clip from his steeplejack work.
3R3-YwDZrzg.why: HN shares it as a dizzying example of Dibnah's fearless chimney work, in threads about heights and climbing.

3TYT1QfdfsM.summary: Rob Miles explains on Computerphile why implementing an off switch for a general AI is hard. A capable agent would resist being stopped because shutdown prevents it from achieving its goal.
3TYT1QfdfsM.why: HN points to it as the standard response to the argument that we can just unplug a dangerous AI.

3byNNUReyvE.summary: Ivan Krstic's Black Hat talk on Apple platform security, including the Find My design that uses elliptic curve key diversification to locate offline devices privately. It also covers hardware features such as the T2 chip and secure boot hardening.
3byNNUReyvE.why: Recommended as a rare insider look at Apple's security architecture and the reasoning behind its hardware choices.

3jQoAYRKqhg.summary: Poul-Henning Kamp's FOSDEM 2014 talk presents a fictitious NSA program called ORCHESTRA, satirizing how intelligence agencies could influence startups and open source. It is a humorous but pointed look at surveillance and subverted software.
3jQoAYRKqhg.why: Recommended as an entertaining talk showing that targeting software projects and introducing bugs is nothing new.

3pvpNKUPbIY.summary: Lex Fridman interviews Instagram co-founder and former CEO Kevin Systrom about building the product, its early days and its pivot story.
3pvpNKUPbIY.why: Pointed to for the founder's own account of Instagram's pivot, early scaling on Django with a small team, and avoiding overengineering.

3qHkcs3kG44.summary: Joe Rogan interviews entrepreneur and angel investor Naval Ravikant on happiness, work, technology platforms, AI and society. Naval revisits ideas from his well-known tweets.
3qHkcs3kG44.why: Mostly cited to support specific points Naval makes, such as platforms and free speech, rather than as a general must-watch.

3wMKoSRbGVs.summary: Lex Fridman interviews Douglas Lenat, founder of Cyc, a decades-long project to encode common-sense knowledge and reasoning for AI. They discuss symbolic AI and how it may complement neural networks.
3wMKoSRbGVs.why: Pointed to as the long-form interview for understanding Lenat's work, especially after his death.

3FAmr1la6w0.summary: A two-minute excerpt of Robert Kennedy's 1968 University of Kansas speech criticizing GDP as a measure of national worth. He notes it counts harmful spending while ignoring what makes life worthwhile.
3FAmr1la6w0.why: HN quotes it whenever debating GDP and metrics of success beyond money.

3UnB1fomvAw.summary: A tool-assisted speedrun of Pokemon Yellow on Game Boy Color that uses glitches and frame-precise inputs to make the game execute an arbitrary program. It was later obsoleted by an improved run.
3UnB1fomvAw.why: HN cites it as a showcase of memory-corruption exploits achievable using only normal controller inputs, often alongside other arbitrary-code-execution speedruns.

3018ABlET1Y.summary: Hillel Wayne reports on interviews with 17 people who have worked as both software and traditional engineers. He argues the fields are fundamentally the same and have much to learn from each other.
3018ABlET1Y.why: HN uses it as the reference for whether software is really engineering and how it differs from other disciplines.

351JCOvKcYw.summary: A PBS Space Time episode on fuzzballs, the string-theory proposal for black holes that replaces the singularity with a tangle of strings. It explains why black holes seem to both have to exist and break known physics.
351JCOvKcYw.why: Cited as an accessible pointer when threads discuss black hole models that avoid singularities.

3AtBE9BOvvk.summary: Tom Scott shows a full-size real-life emoji keyboard built from 14 keyboards and over 1,000 hand-placed stickers, covering all of Unicode 8.
3AtBE9BOvvk.why: Mentioned as a delightful stunt whenever emoji input or keyboards come up.

3BA5bw1EV5I.summary: The Thought Emporium follows up on his earlier video showing negative ion products are radioactive, reporting that Amazon pulled listings and companies shut down. He tests more radioactive quack products with a Geiger counter and cloud chamber.
3BA5bw1EV5I.why: HN points to it as an example of a YouTuber getting radioactive scam products delisted by reporting them to the NRC.

3E9ga-CylWQ.summary: A 36C3 talk that systematically evaluates OpenBSD's exploit mitigations, asking how effective they really are and what they cost in performance, complexity and inspectability. It challenges the project's security marketing.
3E9ga-CylWQ.why: Cited in OpenBSD threads as a skeptical, evidence-based counterpoint to claims about its security, though some dispute its objectivity.

3HYw6vPR9qU.summary: A PBS Space Time episode on how gravitational wave observations of a neutron star merger, GW170817, can limit the number of spacetime dimensions. It is based on a 2018 paper.
3HYw6vPR9qU.why: HN points to it as a clear explanation of the evidence that gravity does not propagate into extra dimensions.

3KdlJlHAAbQ.summary: A one-minute clip of Steve Jobs saying Microsoft has no taste. It is vintage interview footage about design and product sensibility.
3KdlJlHAAbQ.why: HN drops it into Microsoft threads as a quick, quotable jab that people feel still holds.

3MWpHQQ-wQg.summary: A Fry and Laurie sketch about language, full of absurd phrases and wordplay, which also plays on the distinction between langue and parole.
3MWpHQQ-wQg.why: HN quotes it jokingly when talk turns to nonsense language, and one commenter points out its underlying linguistics.

3MYEtQ5Zdn8.summary: Julia Galef introduces the soldier versus scout metaphor for two approaches to thinking, using the Dreyfus Affair as the illustration. She argues the scout mindset leads to better judgment.
3MYEtQ5Zdn8.why: HN uses it as the source of the scout mindset vocabulary when discussing honest reasoning and conversation.

3UxZDJ1HiPE.summary: An overview of the Quiet Logistics warehouse using Kiva Systems robots, narrated by company executives. The robots bring storage racks to human pickers at stations.
3UxZDJ1HiPE.why: Used to show what Kiva-style warehouse automation actually looks like: simple wheeled robots moving racks to humans.

3bxcc3SM_KA.summary: John Oliver's Last Week Tonight segment on patents and patent trolls, explaining how stockpiled patents and lawsuit threats burden businesses. It features the East Texas venue of Marshall.
3bxcc3SM_KA.why: HN shares it as a humorous but accurate primer on patent trolling and why East Texas is a favored venue.

3eyJIbSgdSE.summary: A short clip of economist Milton Friedman discussing the dynamics of illegal immigration and its relationship with the welfare state. It is part one of two.
3eyJIbSgdSE.why: HN uses it as a reference for Friedman's argument that generous welfare and open immigration are in tension.

3t6L-FlfeaI.summary: A short satirical video, originally titled Broccoli Man, in which an engineer who only wants to serve 5 terabytes gets tangled in Google's internal resource and production processes. It is the source of the phrase about forgetting how to count that low.
3t6L-FlfeaI.why: Used as a shorthand joke for Google-scale bureaucracy and the difficulty of simple tasks at large companies.

3vyNzgOP5yw.summary: Ian Cutress interviews Mike Clark, AMD's chief architect of Zen, about his career since the K5, how Zen began and how CPUs are designed. It also covers the future of AMD.
3vyNzgOP5yw.why: HN commenters point to it as a primary source from the architect of Zen, for example on how little the ISA matters compared to microarchitecture.

30WTWkFe910.summary: A compilation of the best Gavin Belson moments from Silicon Valley seasons 1 to 5, showing the show's self-absorbed tech CEO.
30WTWkFe910.why: Used as a joke whenever a tech executive acts like Belson, surrounded by yes-men or making grandiose claims.

33QdTOyXz3w.summary: A Telegraph news clip of the April 2020 White House briefing in which President Trump wondered aloud about disinfectants and sunlight as coronavirus treatments, prompting a backlash from medical experts.
33QdTOyXz3w.why: HN mostly uses it as a source for what Trump actually said, and commenters argue over whether it was sarcasm or whether the headline was accurate.

34CZjsEI1yU.summary: Official music video for Wind Rose's power metal cover of Diggy Diggy Hole, the dwarven mining song originally written by Yogscast.
34CZjsEI1yU.why: HN mostly drops it as a joke whenever digging, tunnels or Dwarf Fortress come up.

35DSdw7dHjs.summary: A six-minute clip of the famous speech from the 1976 film Network in which the world is described as a corporation. It portrays a world run by corporate interests.
35DSdw7dHjs.why: HN posts it as an enduring, still-relevant artistic depiction of corporate power when discussing finance, tech lobbying and ethics.

39cjZTCay24.summary: Curious Droid surveys vertical take-off and landing rockets that predate SpaceX and Blue Origin, including the McDonnell Douglas DC-X of the 1990s. It shows that propulsive landing has about 60 years of history.
39cjZTCay24.why: HN commenters cite it as evidence that vertical rocket landing was demonstrated long before SpaceX, with the DC-X as the main example.

3D8TEJtQRhw.summary: A short clip from The Empire Strikes Back in which Darth Vader tells Lando 'I am altering the deal, pray I don't alter it any further.'
3D8TEJtQRhw.why: Quoted as a joke when a company or government changes terms unilaterally.

3E0a_60PMR8.summary: A C-SPAN clip of Senator James Inhofe displaying and tossing a snowball on the Senate floor, used as an argument against global warming.
3E0a_60PMR8.why: HN commenters invoke it as a shorthand example of climate denial in politics, in threads about climate records and policy, usually critically.

3EwZQddc3kY.summary: A one-minute scene from the film Enemy of the State showing absurdly implausible image enhancement, with freezing, rotating, zooming and focusing on a video.
3EwZQddc3kY.why: Invoked as a joke whenever AI image reconstruction or enhancement is discussed.

3G_uCbKoG5A.summary: A one-minute clip of Microsoft's Clippy, the Office assistant character, in action.
3G_uCbKoG5A.why: Mostly used as a reference for Clippy as an annoying assistant, including as a precedent for forced AI features.

3KPYIaks1UY.summary: A short CNET demo of Bose's electromagnetic active suspension, which gave a very smooth ride but never reached the market. It shows the system in action.
3KPYIaks1UY.why: HN cites it as the demo of active suspension that was a technical success but a commercial flop.

3S5BLs51yDQ.summary: Apple's short ad for the iPad Pro with iOS 11, pitching it as a computer and suggesting a post-PC world.
3S5BLs51yDQ.why: Cited as evidence that Apple markets the iPad as a general-purpose computer, especially in debates about platform openness.

3SlOXowwC4c.summary: A SAAMI-produced training video for firefighters explaining what happens when sporting ammunition burns, including that unchambered cartridges lack the energy to penetrate much. It includes test footage of ammunition in fires.
3SlOXowwC4c.why: Cited as evidence that ammunition cooking off in a fire is much less dangerous than people assume.

3VJT2JeDCyw.summary: A More Perfect Union report on xAI's data center in Memphis, which residents say burns gas without permits or pollution controls and harms their health.
3VJT2JeDCyw.why: HN mostly cites it critically, as evidence of air pollution from AI data center turbines in Memphis.

3XGAmPRxV48.summary: A short clip from the film Goodfellas featuring the 'Fuck you, pay me' scene, tagged as a lesson in business.
3XGAmPRxV48.why: Posted as a joke reply in threads about unpaid work, ransom, and getting stiffed by clients or employers.

3kxG8uJUsWU.summary: C-SPAN clip of Donald Trump in 2016 saying 'Russia, if you're listening' and hoping they find Hillary Clinton's missing emails.
